marble.name: Area and the distributive property
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Use tiling to demonstrate the distributive property: the area of a rectangle with sides a and (b+c) equals a×b + a×c; use area models to represent the distributive property
marble.prompt: If you wants to work out 6 × 13 by splitting it into 6 × 10 and 6 × 3, can they draw a rectangle divided into two parts to show why that method works?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about measurement in everyday life — telling time to the hour and half-hour, comparing lengths and weights of objects, understanding money, and using time words like yesterday and tomorrow.

misconceptions: Distributes to only one addend: 6×(10+3) = 6×10 + 3 (drops the ×6 on the second part)
Adds the side lengths instead of the region areas (6 + 13, or 10 + 3)
Cannot place the split so the two parts recompose to the whole — a spatial-structuring difficulty
Computes the two sub-areas but forgets to add them into the whole
representations: A partitioned rectangle / area model split into two labelled regions
The open array (regions labelled by dimensions, tiles not all drawn)
The aligned equation a×(b+c) = a×b + a×c written beside the picture
Row-strip cutouts for children still building the row/column structure
authoredAnswer: Interpret: the left region is 6×10 = 60, the right is 6×3 = 18, and together they are the whole rectangle, so 6×13 = 6×10 + 6×3 = 78. Produce: draws a 5×12 rectangle split into 5×10 and 5×2, writes 5×12 = 5×10 + 5×2 = 50 + 10 = 60, with the split at the ten and the factor 5 kept on BOTH sub-rectangles.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: In the produce tier writes 5×12 = 5×10 + 2, or in the interpret tier names the second part '3' rather than '6×3'
wrongAnswers.fix: Return to tiles: show the second sub-rectangle is still 6 (or 5) rows tall, so its area is 6×3 not 3; label the repeated side on BOTH regions.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Sums edge numbers rather than the shaded areas; answer looks like a perimeter or a length total
wrongAnswers.fix: Contrast a length (an edge) with a region (the tiles inside); tile one sub-rectangle so the child counts area, not edges.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: In the produce tier draws overlapping/unequal regions, a split that doesn't total 12, or a horizontal cut that breaks the ×5
wrongAnswers.fix: Do NOT impose the equation on top of a partition they can't yet see; give row-strip cutouts or a pre-drawn grid and let them find where 12 = 10 + 2 falls — this coordinates with array practice and self-corrects.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Finds 5×10 = 50 and 5×2 = 10 but doesn't add them, or gives 50 as the answer to 5×12
wrongAnswers.fix: Scaffold: 'You found the two parts — now what is the WHOLE rectangle worth?' — a prompt to complete, not a reteach.

before.name: Area of rectangles by multiplication
before.reason: Must multiply side lengths for area before using area models for distributive property

after.name: Connecting multiplication, fraction and decimal representations
